messages:
incident-bot: Pager: GPU OOM detected on runtime-pool-eu-west-2 (prefill path) — 8 containers restarted in 6m. Priority: P1. @maya is oncall.
maya (oncall): ack — joining. any immediate customer impact?
sam (sre): seeing repeated CUDA OOMs during prefill when requests include ~150k-token context. containers get restarted by oom_killer. logs: `CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY: cuMemAlloc failed`
liam (ml-runtime): adding more detail — KV cache growth spike during prefill + long prompt concat. telemetry shows KV cache > 42GB on some tasks (we expected ~18GB).
nora (customer-ops): one customer reported streaming disconnects and 5xxs for ~3k sessions (GameChat). I flagged their account and started a support ticket.
maya (oncall): mitigation idea: enable eager kvcache eviction on affected hotpool and fallback prefill to partial-streaming. can we do that safely?
sam (sre): I can flip the flag on pool nodes: `PATCH /pools/hotpool/flags {"eager_kv_evict": true}` — will force older prefixes out during prefill. doing a rolling change now, will target 4 nodes first.
liam (ml-runtime): also propose soft-fallback to model-small-prefill for requests > 64k tokens (transparent to app via routing policy). I can push routing rule: `if prefill_length > 64k -> model: gptx-small-prefill`
sam (sre): rolling change started. first 4 nodes toggled, containers stabilized on those. still seeing 2 noisy nodes, isolating now.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: rollout.patch applied to runtime-hotpool (nodes 12-15). status: success for 3/4, 1 failing due to kernel alloc error.
maya (oncall): update customer-ops and incident channel. Nora, please share temp mitigation message with GameChat (explain degraded streaming, active mitigation, ETA 2h).
nora (customer-ops): message drafted and sent to GameChat CSM. they asked for ETA and if data lost — confirmed no user data lost, only transient disconnects. they will loop legal for SLAs.
liam (ml-runtime): found one pattern: requests that include base64-encoded logs expand tokenization wildly causing unexpected kv blowup. filing prompt-safety rule to detect and truncate large blobs.
sam (sre): noisy node isolated and drained. restarted container with `--reserve-kv=48GB` backoff removed. post-change logs show reduced OOMs.
maya (oncall): customer visible impact: high for GameChat (partial outages), low for others (increased latency). current status: mitigations applied (eager kvcache eviction, routing soft-fallback). still monitoring. next steps: follow up memory profiler, add prefill circuit-breaker, add tokenization heuristics. handing off to night oncall in 2h: @alex (oncall-night) + liam for runtime.
ops-bot: Incident annotated: actions: [eager_kv_evict toggle, routing soft-fallback, node drain], ticket created: INC-2026.
maya (oncall): handing off — feel free to DM for context. closing pager for me.
liam (ml-runtime): added follow-up PRs and tests for truncated prefill streaming. will sync in postmortem.
sam (sre): note for postmortem: correlate prefill tokenization spikes + recent client that started sending embedded logs last week. potential short-term fix: enforce max_prefill_bytes per request.
ops-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring.
notes: This thread captures a live pager, immediate mitigations (eager kvcache eviction, routing fallback), customer notification, and on-call handoff. Includes kernel/CUDA OOM details and follow-ups for memory profiling and prompt-safety rules.
